input: Prep a professional development plan for next year

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Professional development can mean technical skills, leadership, soft skills, certifications, networking, or all of the above — knowing the focus areas completely changes what goes into the plan.
Whether this plan is self-directed, co-created with a manager, or presented to HR/leadership affects the tone, depth, and format required.
The user's current role, industry, and career stage determine which goals are realistic and relevant — a junior developer's plan looks nothing like a mid-career marketing manager's.
Available time per week and budget for courses, events, or coaching directly limit what can realistically be planned.
Knowing what 'a great plan' means to the user — a promotion, a career pivot, mastering specific skills, or personal growth — determines what outcomes to optimise for.
Some people prefer learning through courses and certifications; others through on-the-job projects, mentorship, or books — the preferred learning style shapes every recommendation.
The intended format (a simple doc, a structured template, a presentation) and whether this needs to be submitted by a specific date affect how the output is structured and prioritised.

gold.taskTitle: Build a Professional Development Plan for Next Year
gold.taskDescription: Create a structured, actionable professional development plan covering goals, skills, and milestones for the upcoming year.

questions.title: What specific area of growth does this plan focus on?
questions.description: Identify whether the plan targets technical skills, leadership, certifications, soft skills, networking, or a combination — this defines the entire scope of the plan.

questions.title: Who is the primary audience for this plan?
questions.description: Determine whether the plan is purely personal, shared with a manager during a review, or submitted formally to HR or leadership — this shapes tone and required detail.

questions.title: What is your current role, industry, and career stage?
questions.description: Understand where the user sits professionally right now so that goals, benchmarks, and skill recommendations are realistic and relevant.

questions.title: What is your desired outcome by the end of next year?
questions.description: Clarify the north-star result — earning a promotion, pivoting to a new field, mastering a tool, or something else — so the plan is built backwards from a clear target.

questions.title: How much time per week can you realistically dedicate to development?
questions.description: Weekly capacity is a hard constraint that determines how many goals, courses, and activities can be scheduled without the plan becoming unrealistic.

questions.title: How do you learn best — courses, projects, mentorship, or reading?
questions.description: The user's preferred learning modality determines which types of activities and resources the plan should prioritise.

questions.title: What format does the final plan need to be in?
questions.description: Establish whether the deliverable is a simple written document, a structured template with milestones, a slide deck, or another format — and whether there is a deadline for completing it.
